case: Users know how but lack practice time; two prior changes have poor sustained adoption, new tool is installed. Diagnose Ability and fatigue using evidence, propose workload/support interventions, distinguish installation/compliance from adoption; no invented fixed timeline.
required_methods: Identify process, organizational, strategic or culture change, sponsor, honest purpose, affected people/agents and available evidence. Inventory concurrent changes, absorption, workload and ability to pause; diagnose fatigue before proposing another rollout.

Use ADKAR as an evidence-labeled diagnostic: awareness of why, desire/concerns, knowledge of how, ability/time/tools/support and reinforcement. Separate perception from observed behavior and flag missing evidence.

Diagnose vocal and silent resistance, valid objections, timing, lack of consultation, trust and capacity. Adapt the change when objections expose a real defect; do not treat resistance as a personality failure or assume silence is agreement.

Choose interventions for the diagnosed gap and change type: sponsor explanation, participation, targeted training, protected practice time, support and sustained reinforcement. Coordinate communication with its distinct skill and technical implementation with Eric; upstream timelines/thresholds are illustrative only.

Define adoption, usage, reversion, satisfaction, support and outcome measurements with baseline, period, owner and agreed criteria. Distinguish compliance under observation from sustained adoption; record lessons and authorized next actions without independently removing systems or imposing policy.
